topics.label: Lecture welcome and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the audience and states what the lecture aims to cover before introducing its subject matter.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how surgery removes accessible tumors and radiotherapy damages tumors at targeted sites, including how these approaches may be combined with chemotherapy.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: mechanisms and limitations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cytotoxic drugs damage cancer cells, their effectiveness, and the toxicity and resistance that limit their use.

topics.label: Blocking hormone dependence in breast and prostate cancer
topics.groupedBecause: Both examples block hormone signaling that remains necessary for the growth of particular cancers.

topics.label: Exploiting checkpoint and DNA-repair defects in cancer cells
topics.groupedBecause: These approaches use cancer cells’ missing checkpoint or repair functions to make them more vulnerable to treatment.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and genome-guided targeted therapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how identifying the oncogenic events driving a tumor can guide treatments that target the cancer cells’ dependence on those events.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors and resistance to targeted therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how kinase inhibitors block activated kinases and how selectivity problems, resistance, and drug addiction limit their effects.

topics.label: Antibody-based cancer treatments
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics use antibodies that recognize cell-surface targets to direct therapeutic activity against cancer cells.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and checkpoint inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider whether immunity naturally controls cancer and how checkpoint blockade can restore T-cell responses to tumors.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells to attack cancer
topics.groupedBecause: Both approaches direct T cells toward tumor antigens so that they can exert cytotoxic activity against cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer therapy challenges and personalised treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the challenges of treatment and explains how biomarkers and genomic information may help match patients to therapies.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention, and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines changes in cancer rates and how prevention and early detection contribute to those trends.

topics.label: Future cancer treatment priorities and ethical choices
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics consider future treatment priorities and the difficult choices involved in balancing established treatment success against uncertain new therapies and quality of life.
